correctness.rationale: Conditioning gives 1-p+pr^m, whose negative log is additive over independent field samples. With y=cm and alpha=ca/b, the relaxed derivative numerator K=(alpha+y)psi'-psi is strictly decreasing, positive at zero and negative at infinity, giving the unique continuous peak and adjacent integer tie restriction. The log derivative of the adjacent ratio in p is the difference of elasticities (e^z-1)/z at two increasing arguments; it is strictly positive. Using the rightmost maximizer at p=0 in the first-order approximation handles a possible low-availability tie: each adjacent ratio before m0 starts at least one and each from m0 starts strictly below one. At p=1 every adjacent ratio is above one since a>0. A descending pair followed by an ascending pair and three consecutive ties both contradict the strict peak, so thresholds are strictly ordered and no indices are skipped. Bounded H_m for fixed p<1 rules out threshold accumulation below one. At 1-p=k r^m/m, the adjacent difference tends to -ca/b+k(r^(-1)-1), yielding the stated switch coefficient by bracketing. The stationary equation R=psi/psi'-y has R_y>0 and R_epsilon=e^y(psi-p(1-e^(-y)))>0 when epsilon=(1-p)/p, so its root increases with p. On the line y=log(1/epsilon)-log log(1/epsilon)+t, K tends to alpha-e^t, which proves the negative log-log correction. The p=1 objective increases to c/b without a finite optimizer. A separate bounded integer-power bisection for a=b=1 and q=1/2 reproduced the three 12-decimal switching examples; it does not establish the parameter-uniform assertions. The bundled checker was inspected, not executed. Integer field-budget floors, imperfect capture independence and false positives remain outside scope.

evidence: Moore et al. vary the number and duration of field surveys under stochastic visit-specific detectability and travel costs. Buxton et al. explicitly vary both field sample count and technical replicate count in an occupancy simulation, assessing bias and credible interval width for occupancy and observation errors.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Moore's continuous effort tradeoff does not include this integer nested Bernoulli optimum or its sharp adjacent switches. Buxton's optimization is not an exponent-per-cost problem at a known occupied site and admits false positives. Its statement does not give an exact parametric switching law for this loss.

originality.rationale: The hierarchical observation model and the tradeoff between fixed collection costs and within-sample effort are already known. The narrow contribution is the all-index phase diagram for the specified log-miss-per-cost loss, the sharp switch accumulation constant, and the matching continuous high-capture asymptotic. Prior applied optimization does vary laboratory replication, but the closest inspected objectives are materially different.
residual_risks: An earlier exact analysis of the same nested Bernoulli objective may be unindexed or appear outside eDNA under another sampling-design name. Some close applied papers were accessible only as abstracts.

value.rationale: A locally diminishing return to laboratory replication does not by itself locate the global integer switches. The full staircase and its calibrated accumulation rate identify when a single additional technical test changes the most efficient allocation in an idealized detection study. The log-log correction explains the rate at which the preferred count grows as the field availability ceiling disappears. This is useful model insight, not a finite-budget recommendation or an operational laboratory protocol.
